title: Mortgage Servicing Manual, Home Mortgage Loans: Interest in Arrears and the Composition of a Monthly Installment
content:
Interest on a Home Mortgage Loans note is paid in arrears, month by month.

**Clause 1. Interest on an installment.** The interest carried by an installment is the principal balance as it stood after the prior installment was applied, multiplied by the note rate divided by 100 and divided by 12, the result rounded half-up to the cent.

**Clause 2. What a full installment is.** A full installment is the principal and interest payment together with the monthly escrow deposit.

**Clause 3. Interest on a payoff.** Interest on a payoff is computed daily, running from the due date of the last installment, at the note rate divided by 100 and divided by 365.

## The clauses set out as inputs and result

| Quantity | Inputs it is taken from |
|---|---|
| Interest carried by an installment | The principal balance after the prior installment was applied; the note rate divided by 100 and divided by 12 |
| A full installment | The principal and interest payment; the monthly escrow deposit |
| Interest on a payoff | The days running from the due date of the last installment; the note rate divided by 100 and divided by 365 |

## Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

Take a loan whose principal balance stood at $300000.00 after the prior installment was applied and whose note rate is 6.000 percent. The rate divided by 100 is six hundredths, and six hundredths divided by 12 is five thousandths. Five thousandths of $300000.00 is $1500.00, which falls on the cent and needs no rounding. That is the interest carried by the next installment.

Suppose the principal and interest payment on that same loan is $1798.65 and the monthly escrow deposit is $300.00. A full installment is then $2098.65.

For payoff interest, take a loan whose balance is $365000.00 at a note rate of 6.000 percent. Six hundredths of $365000.00 is $21900.00 over a year, and that figure divided by 365 gives $60.00 for each day running from the due date of the last installment. Twelve such days carry $720.00 of payoff interest.
